title: UAE SME e-invoicing readiness consultancy
summary: An independent service would audit invoice data, map accounting-system gaps and help smaller UAE businesses select an accredited provider before mandatory e-invoicing begins for them.
rationale: The compliance deadline and implementation work are real, but the generic opportunity has no defensible wedge: the Ministry of Finance already lists 90 accredited providers, including accounting, tax and software firms that can combine readiness work with implementation. A separate intermediary lacks a clear reason to win distribution or trust.

title: Accessibility remediation workflow for small US municipalities
summary: A managed workflow would inventory websites, mobile apps and public documents for smaller local governments, prioritize WCAG 2.1 AA remediation, coordinate human review and maintain evidence for the federal compliance deadline.
rationale: The Department of Justice gives Title II entities serving fewer than 50,000 people until April 26, 2028 to meet WCAG 2.1 AA, while the Census Bureau reports thousands of municipal and township governments. The payer is the local government responsible for compliance, and W3C warns that tools alone cannot determine accessibility, leaving a specific wedge for inventory, human-reviewed remediation and evidence management rather than another scanner. A manual audit of public sites can test demand cheaply, and no obvious legal or technical constraint kills a services-first pilot.

title: Simpler Recycling compliance app for English micro-firms
summary: A lightweight app would guide English micro-firms through waste-stream checks, bin and collection planning, staff instructions and compliance records before the Simpler Recycling deadline.
rationale: The deadline and enforcement risk are real: micro-firms must comply by 31 March 2027 and can receive Environment Agency compliance notices. The generic app is discarded because the government already directs businesses to Defra-funded sector guidance and a waste calculator, while WRAP provides a five-step setup guide, calculator and downloadable resources. Businesses must still pay a registered waste collector for the operational service, leaving no clear reason for a micro-firm to buy a separate general-purpose compliance app.

nextStep: Reopen only if interviews with 20 micro-firms in one operationally complex vertical reveal a recurring coordination or evidence problem that collectors and the free WRAP tools do not solve; require three commitments to a paid manual pilot before building software.

title: CRA incident-reporting readiness workspace for EU software makers
summary: A lightweight workspace would help smaller commercial software manufacturers identify reportable Cyber Resilience Act events, assemble product and vulnerability facts, run the 24-hour and 72-hour workflow, and preserve a review trail before authorized staff submit through ENISA's official platform.
rationale: The opportunity qualifies because CRA reporting duties for actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents have applied since 11 September 2026, with an early warning due within 24 hours and fuller notification within 72 hours. The payer is the manufacturer responsible for the affected digital product. ENISA explicitly permits automation of internal reporting workflows but provides no API in the platform's initial release, creating a narrow wedge for readiness, evidence assembly, approvals and deadline control without replacing the official submission channel. A tabletop service can test the workflow cheaply, and no obvious legal or technical constraint prevents a non-submitting, human-reviewed product.

title: DROP deletion orchestration for California data brokers
summary: A managed connector would help California data brokers move DROP deletion lists through identifier standardization, internal data stores, downstream service providers, recurring suppression checks and status reporting without replacing the state's official platform.
rationale: The opportunity qualifies because California data brokers have had to process DROP requests since 1 August 2026, normally at least once every 45 days, and the official workflow requires downloading requests, standardizing and hashing records, matching, deletion and status reporting. The regulations extend the work beyond a simple API call: matched personal information must be deleted, service providers and contractors must be directed to delete, and unmatched requests must be checked against newly collected records before sale or sharing. The identifiable payer is the regulated data broker, while the state supports either an API or manual exchange, creating a narrow wedge for orchestration and evidence across the broker's systems rather than a competing request portal. A shadow processing exercise can test the workflow cheaply, and no obvious legal or technical constraint prevents a human-reviewed integration product.

nextStep: Run a manual shadow batch with 15 California data brokers, mapping one DROP list through internal records, downstream vendors and suppression controls; continue only if three agree to pay for a human-reviewed pilot before a production connector is built.

title: Battery passport readiness workspace for EU e-bike importers
summary: A readiness workspace would help importers placing e-bike, e-moped and e-scooter batteries on the EU market collect supplier data, determine field applicability, validate passport records and coordinate QR-code and registry handoff before the 2027 mandate.
rationale: The opportunity qualifies because each light-means-of-transport battery placed on the EU market must have a battery passport from 18 February 2027, and the economic operator placing the finished battery on the market is responsible for keeping its information accurate, complete and current. Commission guidance consolidates 71 potentially relevant data points and explicitly points organisations toward aligning internal processes, data systems and reporting practices. The identifiable payer is the importer responsible for the finished battery, while the decentralised technical model leaves a narrow wedge for supplier-data intake, applicability mapping, validation and evidence management rather than a generic QR generator or replacement for the EU registry. A manual SKU-mapping service can test the workflow cheaply, and no obvious legal or technical constraint prevents a human-reviewed readiness product.

nextStep: Map the official data fields for 10 battery SKUs across 15 EU e-bike or scooter importers; continue only if three agree to pay for a human-reviewed readiness pilot before a hosted passport product is built.

title: Prior-authorization API conformance workspace for US health plans
summary: A managed test workspace would help CMS-regulated health plans exercise required prior-authorization API behavior across payer, provider and EHR workflows, document failures and preserve readiness evidence before the 2027 compliance date.
rationale: The opportunity qualifies because impacted Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, CHIP and federally facilitated exchange plans generally must implement a FHIR-based Prior Authorization API beginning 1 January 2027, including documentation requirements, request and response handling, specific denial reasons and authorization end conditions. CMS says real-world workflow, technical and operational barriers still slow adoption and is using an early-adopter initiative to close workflow gaps and technical handoffs. The identifiable payer is the regulated health plan, while the narrow wedge is independent conformance and end-to-end workflow testing rather than another production authorization platform. A fixed-scope tabletop and synthetic-data test can falsify demand cheaply, and no obvious legal or technical constraint prevents a human-reviewed readiness service that handles no live patient data.

title: Identity-check evidence workspace for UK company formation agents
summary: A lightweight evidence and quality-control workspace would help smaller Authorised Corporate Service Providers complete every Companies House identity-verification step, cover gaps left by commercial identity tools and retain a defensible seven-year record.
rationale: The opportunity qualifies because Companies House requires authorised agents to complete every step of its identity-verification standard, remain responsible when a commercial provider performs only part of the check and keep document copies and check records for seven years. Companies House can request the records, and non-compliance can lead to an offence, fines, prosecution or suspension that stops the agent filing or verifying clients. The identifiable payer is the accounting, legal or company-formation firm acting as an Authorised Corporate Service Provider, while the narrow wedge is evidence completeness, review and request readiness rather than another biometric or document-checking engine. A retrospective file audit can test demand cheaply, and no obvious legal or technical constraint prevents a human-reviewed workflow that leaves the verification decision with the agent.

title: Federal software attestation workspace for US SaaS vendors
summary: A compliance workspace would help smaller software vendors selling to US federal agencies map secure-development evidence to NIST practices, complete a common attestation and reuse the record across procurements.
rationale: The generic opportunity is discarded because its central premise is outdated. OMB Memorandum M-26-05 rescinded the government-wide memoranda that required agencies to obtain secure-software attestations and says agencies are no longer required to collect standardized attestations or use a common form. Agencies may instead tailor risk-based contract terms, while NIST describes the Secure Software Development Framework as recommendations rather than a checklist. CISA still publishes an attestation form, but the form does not restore a uniform mandate. Without a recurring common requirement, the payer, workflow and evidence package fragment by agency and contract, leaving no stable wedge for a general-purpose compliance product.

evidence.title: OMB Memorandum M-26-05: Adopting a Risk-based Approach to Software and Hardware Security
NIST SP 800-218: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1
Secure Software Development Attestation Form

nextStep: Reopen only as an agency- or contract-specific service after reviewing 30 live solicitations and interviewing 15 federal software suppliers; continue only if one repeated evidence package appears and three suppliers agree to pay for a manual pilot.

title: EUDI Wallet payment conformance workspace for EU payment providers
summary: A managed test workspace would help banks and payment service providers validate EU Digital Identity Wallet strong-customer-authentication flows across national wallets, preserve versioned evidence and rerun regressions as standards and implementations change.
rationale: The opportunity qualifies because the European Commission says covered service providers, including payment service providers, must accept EU Digital Identity Wallets for strong customer authentication when users request them by the end of 2027. Commission testing is already exercising production-bound wallets, issuers and readers under peer-to-peer conditions specifically to find interoperability problems, while its payment guidance says technical specifications remain subject to change. The identifiable payer is a non-small bank or payment provider that owns the relying-party integration. The narrow wedge is continuous cross-wallet regression, verifier-version evidence and release readiness rather than another wallet, identity provider or certification scheme. A manual test sprint against reference and partner wallets can falsify demand cheaply, and no obvious legal or technical constraint prevents a human-reviewed conformance service.

title: Age-assurance regression workspace for US mobile app publishers
summary: A cross-platform test workspace would help mobile app publishers exercise state-specific age-band, parental-consent and significant-change flows across Apple and Google APIs, preserve release evidence and rerun regressions as operating-system behavior changes.
rationale: The opportunity qualifies because enacted US state regimes now assign developers operational duties after app stores provide age or consent signals. Louisiana requires developers to verify age categories, obtain parental consent for significant changes and notify app stores, while Google documents regional developer requirements in Texas, Utah and Louisiana. Apple documents state-specific behavior and multiple API changes across OS 26.2, 26.4 and 26.5, creating a material release-testing problem rather than a one-time policy task. The identifiable payer is a mobile app publisher distributing covered apps in those states. The narrow wedge is synthetic cross-platform regression, consent-state simulation and versioned evidence without collecting identity documents or replacing the stores' age-assurance systems. Sandbox test plans can falsify demand cheaply, and no obvious legal or technical constraint prevents a human-reviewed testing product.

nextStep: Run synthetic release-readiness exercises with 15 youth-facing app publishers across Apple and Google state-specific test environments; continue only if three pay for a fixed-scope pilot that catches consent-state or version-regression failures their current QA misses.

title: Data Act switching regression workspace for EU SaaS providers
summary: A managed test workspace would help SaaS providers serving EU customers exercise export and provider-switching workflows, document open-interface and machine-readable-format behavior, and retain versioned evidence as products and interoperability specifications change.
rationale: The opportunity qualifies because the EU Data Act has applied since 12 September 2025 and covers software delivered as a data processing service. Providers must remove switching obstacles, offer open interfaces and at least machine-readable export, while switching and data-egress charges must disappear from 12 January 2027. The Commission also says harmonised interoperability specifications are still being developed to close a current standards gap. The identifiable payer is the SaaS provider responsible for its customer-switching workflow. The narrow wedge is repeatable synthetic export, transition and evidence testing rather than legal advice or a migration marketplace. A fixed-scope portability drill can test demand cheaply, and no obvious legal or technical constraint prevents a human-reviewed conformance service.
